newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE CATTLE END UP ON SHORT COVERING, FUND BUY.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE CATTLE END UP ON SHORT COVERING, FUND BUY.

text.p: CME live cattle futures erased early losses and ran up to day's highs late to close higher. Spillover support also turned feeders mixed, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.500 to 0.100 cent per lb higher with August up 0.150 at 66.575 cents and October was up most at 70.000 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.200 cent higher to 0.050 lower with September off 0.050 at 80.200 cents.

Fund buying added to short covering from an oversold condition to push live cattle up. October paced the advance after holding chart support early and prices rose despite weakness in cash markets and delivery concerns , traders said.
"The cash news does not sound real good right now," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.
October through February also had speculative buying prompted by longer-term bullish ideas, traders said.
They noted the market appeared to be looking ahead to reduced on-feed supplies. Placements of cattle are likely falling below year-ago levels which will tighten cattle numbers later, they added.
Refco, Cargill Investor Services and ING bought October while R.J. O'Brien notably bought February, traders said. Spreaders bought October and sold December and February.
In live cattle options, commercials sold the October 68 put/71 call strangle. Commission houses bought October 72 calls. Commercials were hedging December and February late, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle recovered late following the rally in live cattle which offset pressure from higher corn futures, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index fell $0.25 to $82.31 per cwt.
Prudential Securities sold August while Refco spread long October/short August, traders said. Cargill spread long November feeders/short April live cattle, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures recovered somewhat from early limit losses as commercial demand offset local selling sparked by talk of lower cash boneless beef prices. Weakness in boneless was partly blamed on increased cow slaughter, they said.
"Cows are starting to move (to market) - it's a little dry in some areas and this cow slaughter has picked up some," Tippens said.
But commercial demand developed on expectations the boneless beef average will hold closer to 100 cents then to 90 cents.

Rumors of cash boneless beef sales in the low- to mid-90-cent area may not change the average much if the volume of sales at those levels is low. The average is based on a five-day average and there are only 12 business days to go before August goes off the board, they added.

Boneless beef futures closed 1.80 to 1.20 cent lower with August off most at 98.60 cents per lb after being down as much as the 3.00 cent limit early. October was also off the limit early before ending 1.20 lower.
Trimmings futures followed boneless beef values early but also recovered to end mixed, off 0.50 cent a lb to up 1.50 with August off 0.50 at 45.00 cent.
